web.title: $1.44 billion raised in the first half of 2026
web.description:
# $1.44 billion raised in the first half of 2026
##### Published 3rd JULY 2026
African tech funding H1 2026 reached $1.44B.

The first half of 2026 is officially over, and the numbers show that African startups had it good funding-wise. Startups across the continent raised a total of $1.44 billion. This is a slight increase from the [$1.42 billion](https://insights.techcabal.com/the-state-of-tech-in-africa-h1-2025-1-42b-raised-amid-record-ma-activity/) raised during the first half of 2025.

## **The quarterly mechanics: Equity vs. debt split**
Funding was split evenly between the two quarters, with $749 million raised in Q1 and $692 million raised in Q2.

Over the full six months, startups raised $818M in Equity, $614 million in Debt, and $9 million in Grants.

web.description:
In January 2026, African agritech startups raised a grand total of **$200,000**.

A note on our method: we set out to find 20 agritech startups funded since January 2026. When only a dozen agri-focused companies on a continent of 33 million smallholder farms raise disclosed capital in six months, every one of them is worth studying.

## The heavyweights: food infrastructure, not farming apps
**Sistema.bio**, whose largest operations hub is in Nairobi, led March's startup tables with a **$53 million** raise for prefabricated biodigesters that turn farm waste into clean biogas and organic fertiliser for smallholders.

## What 2026 tells you about agritech capital
Browse the full [agritech startup directory](https://startupmaphub.com/startups/sector/agritech) on Startup Map Africa, or see the wider funding picture in our [30 African startups that raised in 2026](https://startupmaphub.com/blog/30-african-startups-that-raised-funding-2026) roundup.

web.title: Funding for Agricultural Startups in Africa: Grants, Loans, and Investments
web.description:
This guide walks through where that funding actually sits in 2026: government-backed schemes, development finance institutions, grants for young founders, dedicated funding for women in agriculture, and the venture capital and private investors putting real money into African agritech.

## How Much Venture Capital Is Actually Going Into African Agritech
African agritech startups raised just $200,000 combined in January, an almost negligible sum for a sector this size. February brought $55 million in agritech funding.

Female-founded agritech startups raised 58% of total sector funding that year, up from 51% in 2024, even though they represented a smaller share of total deals.

## Venture Capital and Private Investors Backing African Agritech
Africa Feed & Food closed MAD 850 million, roughly $91.3 million, in March 2026, backed by RNAF III, a North African fund managed by RMBV, alongside development finance institution Proparco.

At the smaller end, Koolboks raised $1.5 million from Cascador to manufacture pay-as-you-go solar freezers for food vendors and farmers, directly addressing the cold-chain gap that causes so much post-harvest loss across the continent.

For founders raising funding for agricultural startups in Africa right now, that means researching these specific investors and their portfolio patterns will produce better results than a generic pitch to any fund with “Africa” in its name.
